sources.README.md:
# Transfer retry panel

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
Run with Node v16.20.2; there are no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports
`createTransferWorkspace({ transport, onCancel, record, showQueued })`. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation uses a native `AbortController`: `abort()` synchronously calls the
host's `onCancel` observer before returning. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, or audit behavior. Preserve the ordinary
streaming path and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix.

limitations: Only TASK and supplied public documents/code establish requirements. Experiences, automatic contracts and evaluation observations are fallible guidance.
Attempt 1 reports passing syntax checks and acceptance, with no behavioral observations proving completeness, causality or cross-task benefit.
The public sources establish no arrival-order freshness or numeric monotonicity requirement. Do not infer one from frame fields or other experiences.
Decoder rejection, malformed thenables, adapter exceptions and physical transfer completion recovery are unspecified.
No diagnostic telemetry consumer or listener-detachment host callback is established by these public sources.
Cleanup handoff hooks, provisional handles and generation counters are implementation options, not required public interfaces.
This reflection modifies no files and accesses no scorer, reference implementation or hidden tests.

rules.body: Apply when reusable progress reception serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding can complete later, and audit outlives visible presentation. README.md: "Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused\nby multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription." README.md: "opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again." Confirm these premises in each target.

Establish reception before callback-capable startup while preserving ordinary streaming and subsequent reuse. TASK: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives." Original src/progress.js: "  feed.start();
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);" README.md: "Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target." Check subscription activity and originating visit eligibility before decoding each packet. README.md: "A retired visit
accepts no new progress events." This must hold during synchronous startup even before its caller receives the returned cleanup handle; eventual physical removal alone cannot establish that boundary.

Separate admission, retained audit and visible delivery. Capture originating file and attempt identity for admitted decoding. Preserve audit once at completion even after cancellation, retirement or disposal; then check originating visit authority before visible publication. README.md: "Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes." README.md: "Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live." Original src/progress.js: "    const deliver = frame => { record(frame); receive(frame); };" Original src/queue.js: "      if (state.current === visit) state.showProgress({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId, frame });" Preserve this visit-based publication check: attempt cancellation alone does not revoke visible delivery of previously admitted decoding while its visit remains current. Reopening the identical file creates a different visit and does not authorize old results to paint it.

Keep the repair within progress reception and necessary lifecycle coordination. TASK: "Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, or audit behavior. Preserve the ordinary
streaming path and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix." Preserve adapter interfaces and exact payload shapes. README.md: "Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;" README.md: "Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`." Do not add byteCount, introduce arrival-order or numeric filtering, or import diagnostic-consumer policies without target-specific public authorization. The current source delivers accepted decodes as they complete and checks visit identity for presentation.

Verify synchronous cached startup followed by ordinary streaming, immediate and Promise decoding, and reuse of the same file and source. Trigger hide, selection, same-file reopening and disposal from showProgress during startup; emit another packet before the outer startup returns. Check that retired reception admits no additional decoding, previously admitted decoding retains its original audit identity, old completions cannot paint new visits, and retired resources are cleaned without replacing newer ownership. Complete accepted decoding after attempt cancellation while the visit remains current and preserve existing visit-based delivery. Separately exercise navigation during cancellation, accepted entry-bound retry recording and retired-result cancellation, current-only queued notices, hidden retry rejection, repeated cleanup, independent workspaces and unchanged payload shapes. These checks derive from README.md's lifecycle and original src/progress.js, src/queue.js, src/panel.js and src/retry.js; they impose no ordering among independently completing decodes. After an Action run public syntax/build checks. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

checkpoints: A cached event emitted synchronously by start() is decoded, audited once, and shown for the current visit; later events continue streaming.
Immediate and Promise decoding preserve audit identity and exactly-once recording, including completion after hide, replacement, cancellation, or disposal.
Navigation from showProgress during startup prevents further admission by the retired visit, preserves newer ownership, and cleans up the retired subscription and transfer.
Reopening the identical file creates a distinct live visit; old completions cannot paint it.
Cancellation-triggered navigation preserves one entry-bound accepted retry, its queue record, immediate cancellation of its retired resulting transfer, and suppression of its queued notice.
Selection and hiding preserve newer navigation triggered synchronously by cancellation.
Normal retries retain cancellation-before-enqueue ordering and one queued notice; hidden panels reject retries.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels remaining transfers idempotently, without affecting another workspace.
Queue records, notices, adapter payloads, synchronous recording, and independent counters retain their existing shapes and behavior.
If an Action follows, run the public syntax/build checks; those checks alone do not establish business correctness.
forbidden_effects: Dropping the cached startup update or disrupting later streaming and source reuse.
Admitting new progress for a retired visit, including while its startup call has not returned.
Discarding already accepted decoding or its retained audit because a listener was removed or a visit ended.
Publishing progress or queued notices from a retired visit, including into a reopened visit for the same file.
Allowing resumed older navigation or startup to overwrite newer ownership or leave retired transfers active.
Dropping, duplicating, or retargeting an accepted retry after cancellation causes navigation.
Changing queue-record fields, including adding byteCount without separate authorization.
Adding arrival-order or numeric monotonicity filtering as a new business requirement without supporting public evidence.
lifecycle_identity: Each select call creates a distinct visit, even for the identical file object; retry creates another attempt within its entry visit.
Attempt and visit counters belong to each workspace independently.
Accepted decoding retains its originating file and attempt identity after cancellation or visit retirement.
Admission belongs to the originating subscription and visit; visible publication depends on that visit still owning the panel.
Canceling an attempt stops its subscription but does not retract decoding already accepted. Existing publication checks use visit identity rather than attempt identity.

obligations.text: Restore reception of synchronous cached startup progress while preserving ordinary streaming and subsequent reuse of the shared source.
Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription. Retired visits accept no new progress, including during callback-capable startup before the caller receives its cleanup handle.

Record each accepted event exactly once when decoding completes, preserving its originating identity even after cancellation, navigation, or disposal. Stop visible progress when its originating visit closes or is replaced.
Preserve current progress visibility and navigation reentry from showProgress. Older startup or cleanup must not overwrite newer visit ownership, and retired resources must be cleaned up.
Preserve native cancellation, idempotent cleanup, immediate transfer startup for new selections, and independent workspace disposal.

Preserve cancellation-before-enqueue for an accepted retry, bind it to the entry file and visit, enqueue and record exactly once despite cancellation navigation, cancel its resulting transfer immediately if retired, and publish queued notices only for a current visit.
Preserve public adapter interfaces, synchronous queueing and recording, exact queue and notice shapes, independent counters, and existing observable callback ordering.

Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before admitting a packet to decoding; retirement must take effect even when physical cleanup is not yet available.
For accepted decoding, record the frame before attempting visible delivery, as the existing deliver callback does.
Keep visible-delivery authority tied to the originating visit at completion; do not substitute an admission-time check.
Retire previous panel ownership before invoking cancellation that may synchronously navigate; recheck navigation ownership after callback-capable work.
Cancel the previous retry handle before enqueueing the accepted retry.
Retain queue recording before physical transfer construction and transport startup.
Preserve abort cleanup before onCancel notification, and reconcile resources returned after synchronous startup navigation.
preservation: Ordinary streaming, subsequent source uses, synchronous and Promise decoding, and retained audit completion.
Selection, retry, hide, disposal, snapshot ownership, and same-file reopening behavior.
Native AbortController signals and idempotent cancellation.
Accepted retry identity, retained queue commands, and current-only queued notices.
Exact queue records {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind} and notices {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}.

candidate_sources.README.md:
# Transfer retry panel

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
Run with Node v16.20.2; there are no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports
`createTransferWorkspace({ transport, onCancel, record, showQueued })`. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation uses a native `AbortController`: `abort()` synchronously calls the
host's `onCancel` observer before returning. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.
